tool_args.rationale: The measured outputs track u_now closely while horizon is varied, consistent with saturating Kelvin–Voigt creep. Fit its positive modulus and rate numerically to all paid rows, and defer further probing because the available batch provides multi-input and horizon coverage.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Eight observations now span several nearby horizons and multiple input levels; the authorized two-parameter creep law is directly fit-able, so further paid data is not justified.
The observed response is nearly proportional to u_now across rows and shows little apparent dependence on x_now, unlike the authorized cooling law's explicit initial-state contribution.
This present-snapshot law does not use horizon and is poorly matched to the stated slow-horizon/damped-transient setting; the creep law captures horizon dependence.
